THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

15-Minute Chicken Tikka Masala Split Plate

Fridge shortcut. 15 min end-to-end. One shared cook, two age-appropriate portions. Adult: 2 servings + 2 rotis + Kashmiri chili (540 cal / 50g protein). Kid: 1.5 servings + 1.5 rotis, deconstructed, mild (405 cal / 38g protein). Split at the pot BEFORE the chili — the mild kid meal never touches the adult heat.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME15 min (7 min pouch warm + 5 min stovetop heat + 3 min split & finish)
COOK METHODStovetop · Assembly
EST. / SERVING~540 cal | ~50g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: SPLIT BEFORE THE CHILI. Remove 3 servings (1.5 per kid) BEFORE stirring 1 tsp Kashmiri chili into the adult portion. Once the chili is in, the kids' portions are gone.

Ingredients

PROTEIN + SAUCE

  • 1 package / 36 oz prepared chicken tikka masala (2 x 18 oz Sukhi's Costco pouches — seven 5 oz servings total)

SHARED

  • Water, hot from the tap (for warming the sealed pouches)

Option 1

  • (NO Kashmiri chili — adult-only)

CARB

  • 7 frozen rumali rotis (~40g each — Vadilal)

ADULT FINISH

  • 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder (stirred into the remaining 4 servings AFTER the kids' portions are out)

Allergens: dairy, gluten. Verify halal package Verify allergens current labels Physical package priority for heating

AT THE POT, BEFORE THE CHILI. All 7 servings warm together in the saucepan; remove 3 servings for the kids' plates BEFORE stirring the 1 tsp Kashmiri chili into the remaining 4 adult servings. The mild kid meal never touches the adult heat.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.WARM THE POUCHES. Place the 2 sealed tikka masala pouches in a bowl of hot tap water. Let sit 5-7 min. THE PHYSICAL PACKAGE TAKES PRIORITY if the directions differ from this general guidance.
  2. 2.EMPTY INTO A SAUCEPAN. Discard the warming water. Cut open the pouches and empty the tikka masala into a saucepan.
  3. 3.PAN-HEAT COVERED. Cover the saucepan and heat on medium-low for about 5 min, stirring once, until the chicken and sauce are steaming hot throughout.
  4. 4.WARM THE ROTIS. While the tikka heats, warm the frozen rotis one at a time in a dry pan 10-15 sec per side (or per the package). Stack under a clean towel to hold soft.
  5. 5.SPLIT POINT — REMOVE KID PORTIONS. Before adding any Kashmiri chili, spoon out 3 total tikka masala servings for the kids' plates (1.5 servings per kid). This is the non-negotiable step — spice doesn't come back out once it's in.

Adult — 2 Tikka Servings + 2 Rotis + Kashmiri Chili

  1. 6.STIR IN KASHMIRI CHILI. With the 4 adult servings still in the pan, sprinkle 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder over the surface and stir to distribute. Heat 30-60 sec covered to bloom the spice.
  2. 7.PLATE THE ADULT. Spoon 2 tikka masala servings onto or next to 2 warmed rumali rotis. Serve immediately. 540 cal / 50g protein.

Kid — 1.5 Tikka Servings + 1.5 Rotis, Deconstructed, Mild · Option 1

  1. 6.PLATE THE KID. Portion 1.5 tikka masala servings into a compartment tray — chicken pieces in one section, extra gravy in a separate ramekin or well, 1.5 warmed rotis torn or halved on the side. Kid controls dipping, assembly, and bite size.
  2. 7.ADJUST TO KID APPETITE. If the kid finishes the 1.5 servings and wants more, dip into the adult pot BEFORE it's been stirred with Kashmiri — hard to do after the split, so watch the split-timing carefully. Otherwise, extend with an extra plain roti (240 cal / 6g protein per whole roti).

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — 2 Tikka Servings + 2 Rotis + Kashmiri Chili: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — 1.5 Tikka Servings + 1.5 Rotis, Deconstructed, Mild: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • WARM POUCHES IN HOT WATER FIRST. 5-7 min in hot water while the rotis thaw. Then empty into a saucepan for the 5-min pan finish. THE PHYSICAL PACKAGE TAKES PRIORITY if directions differ.
  • KID PLATE = DECONSTRUCTED. Chicken + gravy + rotis in separate compartments. Kids reject the mixed-composition plate — they want components they control.

If something fails

I added Kashmiri chili to the whole pot and now the kids won't eat it: Once the chili is in the sauce, it doesn't come out. Options: (a) plate the kids with rotis + plain yogurt / raita on the side, skip the sauce; (b) rinse the chicken pieces briefly in warm water to remove some surface sauce (loses the point); (c) order pizza and learn for next time. SPLIT BEFORE THE CHILI is the single non-negotiable rule of this recipe.

Sauce is scorched or thickened too much on the pan finish: Skipped the hot-water warm step, or the pan heat was too high. The 5-min pan finish should be covered on medium-low, stirring once. Add 1-2 tbsp water or bone broth to loosen; the sauce should be spoonable, not paste-thick.

Rotis are rubbery or dry: Warmed in the microwave in a stack (steam turned them gummy) or over-warmed in the pan (dried them out). Warm one at a time in a dry pan 10-15 sec per side, or per the package. Stack under a clean towel between warming to hold soft.

Kid refuses the deconstructed plate: Try smaller portion sizes first — 1 serving chicken + 1 roti torn into strips + gravy in a separate ramekin. Overloading the tray reads as pressure. Verify the tikka isn't a spicier variety (some Sukhi's flavors are hotter than the classic tikka masala) — check the package heat rating.

Adult plate feels underspiced even with Kashmiri chili: 1 tsp Kashmiri is designed for moderate warmth + red color, not intense heat. Add 1/4 tsp cayenne or a drizzle of hot chili oil to the adult portion after plating. Keep the addition on the adult side of the pot only.

Not enough for hungry adults / bigger kids: The 36 oz twin-pack budgets 7 servings — 2 per adult + 1.5 per kid = 7 exactly. For hungrier eaters, buy a second twin-pack and hold the second package sealed for a repeat later in the week. Or extend with extra rotis (calories are cheap; 240 cal / 6g protein per roti).

Sukhi's isn't available at my Costco: Sub any refrigerated / shelf-stable chicken tikka masala with a comparable macro profile (~150 cal / 22g protein per 5 oz serving). Trader Joe's, Whole Foods 365, or Deep Foods frozen twin-packs all work. Recheck adult / kid macros against the actual package you buy — the 540/50 and 405/38 numbers are Sukhi's-specific.

Storage and reheating

Store: Store any leftover curry and rotis SEPARATELY in sealed containers. Refrigerate promptly. FOLLOW THE PHYSICAL PACKAGE for storage window — if Sukhi's or Vadilal give a shorter guidance than 3-4 days, use their number.

Reheat: Reheat curry covered on the stovetop to 165°F, or microwave 60-90 sec (covered) with a splash of water if the sauce has tightened. Warm rotis separately in a dry pan 10-15 sec per side — don't microwave rotis in a stack (steam makes them rubbery).

Lasts: Curry: 3-4 days fridge (or per the Sukhi's package). Rotis: 2-3 days fridge, or freeze back for longer. Assemble immediately before eating for best texture.

Estimated nutrition

~540 cal | ~50g protein.

15-Minute Chicken Tikka Masala Split Plate

Fridge shortcut. 15 min end-to-end. One shared cook, two age-appropriate portions. Adult: 2 servings + 2 rotis + Kashmiri chili (540 cal / 50g protein). Kid: 1.5 servings + 1.5 rotis, deconstructed, mild (405 cal / 38g protein). Split at the pot BEFORE the chili — the mild kid meal never touches the adult heat.

Make this when

Soccer ended at 6:45. Dinner needs to be on the table at 7. No meal prep, no delivery, no separate kid meal. Refrigerated chicken tikka masala pouches + frozen rumali rotis + one adult-only spice upgrade = a full split-plate dinner in 15 minutes. The pouches warm in hot water while the rotis thaw; you split the kids' portions BEFORE stirring in Kashmiri chili so the mild kid meal never touches the adult heat. This is the emergency dinner the freezer + fridge are stocked FOR.
